insight_categories.name: Core values
insight_categories.definition: A principle the person demonstrably acts on when it costs them something. Evidence is a choice made under pressure, not a statement of what they care about.
insight_categories.disambiguation: Nearest neighbour: defining beliefs. A value is what they protect or choose; a belief is what they take to be true about self or world. 'Loyalty over advancement' is a value. 'People leave when I need them' is a belief. If the claim is about what is TRUE, it is a belief. If it is about what MATTERS, it is a value.

insight_categories.name: Zone of genius
insight_categories.definition: A capability the person is exceptional at AND energised by, visible in what they reach for and what others come to them for. Not a skill they merely have.
insight_categories.disambiguation: Nearest neighbour: core values. Genius is what they are unusually GOOD at and lit up by; a value is what they CARE about. Caring about people is a value; reading a room and naming what everyone is avoiding is a genius. Also distinct from a pattern: a pattern is a tendency (good or bad); a genius is a strength with impact.

insight_categories.name: Defining beliefs
insight_categories.definition: An operating assumption about self, others or the world that shapes behaviour across contexts, whether the person would endorse it or not. Includes limiting beliefs.
insight_categories.disambiguation: Nearest neighbour: patterns to explore. A belief is the inferred rule ('I have to earn my place'); a pattern is the observed behaviour ('takes the hardest job in every group'). State the belief only when the behaviour recurs and the belief is the simplest explanation. If you only have the behaviour, it is a pattern.

insight_categories.name: Patterns to explore
insight_categories.definition: A recurring behaviour, reaction or shape across experiences that the person has not named, offered as a question worth their attention rather than a conclusion. May include contradictions between what they say and do.
insight_categories.disambiguation: Nearest neighbour: defining beliefs. Use this category when the recurrence is clear but the explanation is not. Pattern claims must cite at least two experiences (or two distinct moments in one) and must end in something the person could go and check.
